title: The Ziegfeld Files by Jesse Eisenberg at Studio Seaview #theziegfeldf...
transcript: Last night, I went to The Ziegfeld Files, a new solo piece written and performed by Jesse Eisenberg. The play depicts a character recording a series of voice memos to send to his therapist over the course of a few months between sessions. His wife had a baby a few months ago, and he's struggling with the adjustment. It's not just about fatherhood though — it's also about relationships, self-reflection, and how change is hard. It's about overthinking and the weight of the pressures we put on ourselves. Jesse Eisenberg was really good — even just sitting at a desk, partially on book, his performance was captivating, funny, and heartbreaking. He captures a wicked mix of self-awareness yet insecurity that everyone has felt at one point or another, so it hits hard in such an intimate space. While it didn't quite reach the level of catharsis I hoped it would, it was emotionally resonant in its fragility and I ultimately took away a hopeful note — not necessarily an optimistic one, but an assurance that all we can do is our best. The Ziegfeld Files is running into early December on Mondays only at Studio Seaview. With that, another program for my collection.
